## Hypothesis history

- after step 7: Aurora kinase inhibitors 0.55, Microtubule destabilizers 0.20, Protein synthesis 0.10, Eg5 inhibitors 0.05, Microtubule stabilizers 0.04, DNA damage 0.02, DNA replication 0.01, Kinase inhibitors 0.01, Actin disruptors 0.01, Cholesterol-lowering 0.01, Epithelial 0.01, Protein degradation 0.01

## Conclusion 1

**Aurora kinase inhibitors** (stated probability 0.62); key evidence e3, e4, e2, e5.

Why: Grape-like multinucleation with polyploid large nuclei and low mitotic fraction favors Aurora slippage over destabilizer arrest.

Next experiment if this were a real lab: p-Histone H3 + DNA time-lapse and Aurora pT288 IF across doses to quantify cytokinesis failure/multinucleation vs sustained mitotic arrest and tubulin polymer mass.

## Conclusion 2

**Microtubule destabilizers** (stated probability 0.52); key evidence e12, e3, e4, e5, e13.

Why: Mid-dose-only atlas gives 0 Aurora, top4 demecolcine 0.95-0.97; uncertain: single replicates, microscopist favored Aurora, high-dose atlas splits synthesis/Eg5.

Next experiment if this were a real lab: Replicate 0.03-3uM dose-response with p-H3/tubulin polymer mass IF plus live DNA imaging to distinguish destabilizer mitotic arrest vs Aurora slippage and rule out protein-synthesis mimic; budget spent so no new well here.

## PI review

Verdict: request experiment.

Clean mid-dose multinucleation/polyploidy with low mitotic fraction and little tubulin change favours Aurora over mitotic-arrest classes, but the atlas pooled both wells and found 0 Aurora neighbours (Protein synthesis 6/10, Microtubule destabilizers 4/10), the 10µM phenotype explicitly could not distinguish Aurora/destabilizer/stabilizer/Eg5, both wells are single-replicate, and the 0.55→0.62 increase followed three null dose-response analyses. A free per-well atlas check is decisive and was not done.

Requested: compare_to_reference_atlas on the 0.3 µM well alone (dose index 4, rep 1, w_552fc323cc), not pooled with the 10 µM well — Aurora neighbours would support approval; continued Protein-synthesis/destabilizer-only neighbours would overturn the 0.62 call.

## Unblinding

Compound: **vincristine** (PubChem CID [5978](https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/5978))

Identity check: name and BBBC021 structure agree

ChEMBL mechanisms: Tubulin inhibitor

## Verdict (computed by code)

Correct: agent said **Microtubule destabilizers**, BBBC021 annotates **Microtubule destabilizers**.

## Reflection

Initial high-dose (tub_std z=+21.4) and mid-dose (nuc_solidity z=-43.8, frac_large_nucleus z=+14.3) correctly captured severe nuclear shape loss with large/multinucleated nuclei, and the final per-well atlas correctly overturned Aurora in favor of microtubule destabilizers (PMID 36967563, PMID 19881550).

What misled was overweighting the first microscopist Aurora-only call and the slippage-like interpretation of polyploid large nuclei, while discounting the pooled atlas Protein synthesis 6/10 plus Microtubule destabilizers 4/10 signal; pooling the 10 uM and 0.3 uM wells hid the per-well result and the 10 uM description explicitly could not distinguish Aurora/destabilizer/stabilizer/Eg5.

The acquisition choice to spend the 2-well budget on single replicates at 10 uM and 0.3 uM left all three dose_response checks null, so the 0.55 to 0.62 Aurora increase had no dose-trend support; the reviewer-requested per-well atlas on w_552fc323cc alone with 0 Aurora neighbours was decisive for the correct vincristine tubulin-inhibitor call (PMID 31930676, PMID 26024389).

What was right:
- High-dose tub_std z=+21.4 flagged cytoskeletal disruption consistent with tubulin inhibitor
- Mid-dose nuc_solidity z=-43.8 and frac_large_nucleus z=+14.3 captured multinucleation/polyploidy seen with vincristine
- Second microscopist included microtubule destabilizers in differential despite first Aurora-only call
- Per-well atlas on 0.3 uM alone showed 0 Aurora neighbours with destabilizer matches, correctly overturning Aurora lead

What was wrong or missed:
- Overweighted first describe_phenotype Aurora-only call and slippage interpretation over atlas destabilizer signal
- Used pooled compare_to_reference_atlas across divergent doses which diluted dose-specific neighbours into Protein synthesis 6/10
- Acquired only 2 single-replicate wells leaving dose_response of frac_mitotic_like, nuc_dna_integrated and tub_mean null and inflating confidence 0.55 to 0.62 without trend
- Misread Protein synthesis neighbours as excludable by morphology alone without considering mitotic-arrest mimicry

Proposed next experiment: Replicate 0.03-3 uM vincristine dose-response with phospho-histone H3 plus soluble vs polymer tubulin immunofluorescence and live DNA imaging to quantify sustained mitotic arrest vs slippage/multinucleation and directly measure tubulin polymer loss.

## Citations

Citations verified: 4/4

- PMID [36967563](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36967563/): Destabilization of microrchidia family CW-type zinc finger 2 via the cyclin-dependent kinase 1-chaperone-mediated autophagy pathway promotes mitotic arrest and enhances cancer cellular sensitivity to microtubule-targeting agents. *Clin Transl Med* (2023) — Microtubule-targeting agents promote mitotic arrest and modulate sensitivity to mitotic drugs.
- PMID [31930676](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31930676/): SIRT3, PP2A and TTP protein stability in the presence of TNF-α on vincristine-induced apoptosis of leukaemia cells. *J Cell Mol Med* (2020) — Vincristine induces apoptosis in leukaemia cells in a TNF-alpha modulated pathway.
- PMID [26024389](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26024389/): Identification of synthetic lethality of PLK1 inhibition and microtubule-destabilizing drugs. *Cell Death Differ* (2015) — PLK1 inhibition is synthetically lethal with microtubule-destabilizing drugs.
- PMID [19881550](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/19881550/): LIM-kinase 2, a regulator of actin dynamics, is involved in mitotic spindle integrity and sensitivity to microtubule-destabilizing drugs. *Oncogene* (2010) — Regulators of cytoskeletal dynamics control mitotic spindle integrity and sensitivity to microtubule-destabilizing drugs.
